messages:
sam: Heads-up — p95 for /v1/generate (prod, eu-west) jumped from ~210ms to ~430ms around 10:14 UTC. p50 steady.

tess: saw that on the dashboard too. It's scoped to requests that hit the canary routing policy (weight ~3%).

sam: is p99 moving as well?

tess: p99 ticked up a bit (900ms -> ~1.1s) but much noisier. p95 is the sharper signal.

leo: can we get the cohort breakdown? small-population effects + tdigest rollups can make p95 look worse if sample weights shifted.

maya: ran a quick split by client and model-variant. interesting: majority of the p95 uplift is from requests with header `X-Route: canary-dedicated` and response size > 2k tokens.

sam: that screams kvcache miss amplification. can we check kvcache miss rate around the window?

maya: pasted query: ```
select time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, percentile(lat_ms,95) as p95, sum(kvcache_miss) as miss from traces
where route='canary' and env='prod' and ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' group by t order by t;
```

leo: FYI our console rollups use tdigest for long-term storage and raw samples for the last 1h. Are we sure the panel is showing the raw-sample p95 and not the rolled-up tdigest-derived p95?

sam: good call. The panel in question is the endpoint-percentile viz we added last quarter — I think it falls back to the rollup series when the raw stream is sparse.

tess: samplecount for the cohort is ~1.2k -> 1.18k during spike window, so not extremely sparse. Why would tdigest shift that much?

leo: tdigest is sensitive to weights when ingestion boundaries (buckets) change — routing policy tweak yesterday changed fallback weighting for quantized variants; that changes how many tokens per request get attributed to the rollup.

maya: also noticed a partial rollback of the retry change for the canary earlier today. Some callers still do client-side retries which inflate tail latency at the endpoint level but won't show in backend processing time.

sam: so two hypotheses: (1) kvcache miss on new fallback variant causing real midtail latency; (2) metric derivation differences (tdigest vs raw) + retry amplification making the dashboard p95 look worse than backend p95.

tess: what do we want to validate? I can run an ad-hoc trace correlation and a raw-sample aggregation for the affected minute window.

leo: please add a small sample of request IDs and run `trace_id -> ingress_latency vs model_processing_latency` join. If ingress >> model processing that's retries/queueing. If model processing >> ingress it's backend slowness (kvcache/model variant).

maya: ran that join for 10:13-10:17 UTC: majority show model_processing_latency spike and a ~0.4 increase in kvcache_miss_rate for the canary variant. Attached top-5 trace ids: abc123, def456, ghi789, jkl012, mno345.

sam: nice — that favors the kvcache hypothesis. Can we repro locally by forcing a canary traffic hit with same variant?

maya: attempted `curl` script against canary host with the `X-Route: canary-dedicated` header and a 2.5k token prompt. Observed a 450-500ms median and occasional 1s+ tails.

leo: confirms. Next steps: (a) tag the metrics in the rollout dashboard with `fallback_variant` label so we can slice quickly, (b) add an explicit ``raw vs tdigest`` toggle on the percentile panel, (c) update rollout gating: pause if p95 > 300ms for 5m on canary.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR to add `fallback_variant` to the canary metric emitter and patch the rollout gating rule.

tess: I'll file a console UX issue for a `show raw samples` toggle and a short tooltip explaining tdigest caveats (counts, weights, ingestion boundaries).

maya: FYI created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/issues/1422 — includes the trace snippets and the curl script.

ingest-bot: metric-tags v1.2 deployed to canary at 10:22 UTC (deploy id: deploy-7132).

sam: after the tag deploy, p95 dropped back to baseline within two minutes. Looks like easier to slice now. :+1:

tess: closing the incident for now but please keep the dashboard annotation for the canary rollout and add the tdigest note to docs.

sam: will add a 2-3 sentence blurb to the docs repo and link to the console issue. Also adding an ops checklist item: when you see isolated p95-only spikes, verify whether panel is using tdigest rollups and confirm samplecount + retry delta.

leo: and let's consider exposing both 'raw-sample p95' and 'rollup p95' in the API so downstream teams don't have to guess derivation.

maya: agreed. Thanks everyone.

sam: thanks — great triage.
